title: Abdali Is Alarmed by the Khalsa-Jat Alliance

blocks.text: News of the new alliance spreads quickly through Abdali's camp. Listening about this new development, Ahmad Shah Abdali feel a sharp blow to his confidence, because he knows that any campaign against Jawahar Mal becomes far more dangerous once Sikh horsemen join the field.

The political meaning is obvious to him. The young Khalsa Singhs had joined the Jat chief, and that combination threatens to snatch it from him: the prestige he had gathered after defeating other Indian powers could now be undone by a fresh coalition in the north.

The page therefore emphasizes fear rather than triumph. Instead of striking at once, Abdali grows more scared and panicky, calculating not only the military risks of battle but also the humiliation that would follow if the Singhs helped Jawahar Mal throw him back.
